subject: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up — hosted vs dedicated vs private (ACME Retail)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up — hosted vs dedicated vs private (ACME Retail)

Hi Samir — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from our discovery:
- Use case: real-time chat & personalization for shoppers (avg. prompt 120 tokens; avg. response 380 tokens).
- Peak traffic: expected 80 RPS during promos; baseline 10 RPS.
- Data sensitivity: PII filtered; want SOC2 and audit logs; considering Private VPC for regulated workloads.
- Key ask: guidance on cost tradeoffs across Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private (VPC/on-prem).

Attached is a first-pass cost model (Redwood_Cost_Model_ACME_v1.xlsx) — high level notes below. Happy to walk through these numbers live.

High-level pricing view (ballpark):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): simple, no infra commit. Estimated ~ $0.60 per 1M tokens (combined request+response) with current model choices; best for variable/low baseline traffic.
- Dedicated (reserved commits): monthly reserved capacity pricing — rough example: $22k/month reserved gives predictable throughput (~100 RPS sustained) and lowers effective cost to ~$0.22 per 1M tokens at your expected utilization. Good if you have steady baseline and want unit-cost savings.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): higher up-front/setup cost and support; unit economics depend on utilization and infra amortization. Often comparable to Dedicated at high sustained utilization but adds networking/KMS/compliance benefits.

Open questions for us to finalize the model:
1) Do you expect sustained baseline closer to 10 RPS or is 20-30 RPS more realistic outside promo windows?
2) How much of traffic needs strict VPC-only isolation versus just audit/KMS controls?
3) Acceptable commit term? 12 vs 24 months will change committed rate materially.

Proposed next steps:
- I can schedule a 45-min pricing review with you + procurement + our SE (Marissa) this week to walk the workbook and run sensitivity scenarios.
- If you want a deeper security discussion, we can include Neha for Private/VPC requirements and SOC2 artifacts.

Would Tues or Thurs this week work for a call?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Thanks, Aditya — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Baseline outside promos is closer to 18 RPS; during large promotions we spike up to ~85 RPS for short windows (5-8 minutes).
- We need VPC isolation for any model that stores logs with PII; otherwise audit+KMS for hosted endpoints would be fine for pseudonymized events.
- Procurement prefers to see a 12-month commit; will consider 24 only with larger discounts.

Tues afternoon (EST) works for Marissa + me. Please include the cost workbook and a recommended committed tier.

Best,

Subject: Re: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up — hosted vs dedicated vs private (ACME Retail)

Great — thanks for the clarifications. I've updated the workbook to reflect: baseline 18 RPS, promo spikes to 85 RPS (short duration), and a 12-month commit scenario. See attached PDF summary for a quick read (redwood-dedicated-commit-summary.pdf) and the full Excel. Key takeaways from the updated model: 

1) Hosted (PAYG) — easy to start, no commit: 
   - Cost example: at your traffic profile, estimated monthly tokens ~ 1.4B tokens.
   - Estimated monthly cost (HOSTED mix, current rates): ~$840/month per 100M tokens => ~ $11,760/month for 1.4B (note: that's a simplified roll-up; workbook has line-by-line).
   - Pros: no commit, instant scale; Cons: higher unit cost under sustained usage, less predictable pricing.

2) Dedicated (12-month commit) — reserved capacity economics: 
   - Suggested tier: 1x Reserved Pool sized for 40 RPS sustained (handles baseline + most promo tail with autoscale for peaks).
   - Example pricing: $20,000/month commit yields estimated effective unit cost ~$0.18 per 1M tokens when amortized at expected utilization (see sheet 'Commit sensitivity').
   - With modest autoscale bursts (on-demand credits) to cover short promo spikes, overall effective spend projected ~ $18k-$25k/month depending on burst usage.

3) Private (VPC) — for VPC-only workloads: 
   - Add-on overhead: one-time setup & network config + managed private control plane (~$35k onboarding amortized) and monthly platform fee (~$6-8k).
   - If you commit at a high sustained level (e.g., 60 RPS sustained), Private can approach Dedicated economics; otherwise higher fixed costs dominate.

Action items:
- Confirm Tues 12/8 2:30pm EST for the pricing walkthrough (I've tentatively blocked it).
- Marissa — can you run two sensitivity slides? 1) 12-month commit at 40 RPS, 2) 12-month commit at 60 RPS with expected burst credits.
- Neha — can you pull the PIR for VPC onboarding (network diagram, estimated lead time) so we can share with ACME procurement?

If that sounds right, I'll lock the meeting and send a calendar invite + updated workbook.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
